card.summary: A two‑storey, white‑sided colonial home with a pointy gable roof, red front door, porch, dormer, shutters, and a two‑car garage.
card.description: The new residence is a two‑storey Dutch‑Colonial inspired home measuring 792 cm wide by 853 cm deep with a total height of roughly 530 cm. White wood siding wraps the exterior, punctuated by a pointy gable roof clad in dark asphalt shingles and a prominent dormer that adds visual interest to the roofline. A bright red front door, framed by hinged wooden shutters, welcomes visitors onto a concrete porch that extends 300 cm by 200 cm and is sheltered by its own shingled roof. Six well‑proportioned rooms—including three bedrooms, a sun parlor, a bathroom and a versatile living area—are arranged on two levels with ceiling heights of 259 cm on the first floor and 244 cm on the second. The interior is finished with white paint, timber flooring, and period‑appropriate trim, while modern conveniences such as recessed lighting, a thermostat, and a full set of electrical, plumbing, and HVAC services are discreetly integrated. A two‑car garage sits at the rear, accessed through a sliding metal door, and the home is equipped with eight operable windows, four pairs of shutters, and a set of interior doors that swing on hinges. The design balances historic charm with contemporary livability, delivering a stately yet functional family dwelling.

Finish interior finishes, paint, install fixtures, conduct a final inspection and hand over the completed home.

card.summary: A 1‑storey colonial bungalow (792 × 1417 cm, 250 cm tall) with four rooms, a bathroom, garage, porch, and a front‑door oak coat rack.
card.description: This single‑storey colonial bungalow measures 792 cm wide by 1417 cm deep with a modest 250 cm roofline, echoing the classic 1920s pattern‑book aesthetic. The shingled roof crowns a façade of red‑brick veneer walls, while white-painted wooden trim frames double‑hung windows that rhythmically punctuate the elevation. A solid‑wood front entry door, flanked by a graceful oak coat rack, welcomes visitors onto a concrete porch stepped with subtle detailing. Inside, four well‑proportioned rooms and a centrally located bathroom flow from a simple hallway, each finished with hardwood floors and plastered interior walls. The kitchen boasts maple cabinets and a modest efficiency layout, while the two‑car garage, set to the side, features a sliding steel door. Original colonial elements such as dormer‑style roof peaks and modest porch railings give the home a stately yet homely presence, while modern services—electrical, plumbing, and HVAC—are discreetly integrated. The coat rack, 100 cm tall with five evenly spaced hooks, provides a functional accent at the threshold, reinforcing the house’s welcoming character.

Excavate and pour a 20 cm thick concrete slab foundation with reinforcement, then install anchor bolts for the structural walls.

Install roof trusses, lay asphalt shingles, fit double‑hung windows, and hang the front entry door with a pre‑drilled opening for the coat rack.
Finish interior finishes, connect electrical, plumbing and HVAC services, mount the coat rack, and conduct a final inspection for code compliance.

Roof material is assumed to be asphalt shingles, matching the reference designs.

card.summary: A 1‑storey colonial bungalow of 792 × 1 417 cm with a front‑hall wall mirror provides a classic, reflective entrance.
card.description: This single‑storey colonial bungalow measures 792 cm wide by 1 417 cm deep with a modest 259 cm roofline, echoing the classic 1920s pattern‑book proportions of the Desoto model. The exterior is clad in painted white wood siding, capped by a low‑pitch asphalt shingle roof that shelters a simple front entry door and eight double‑hung windows with operable sashes. Inside, a spacious front hall greets visitors, its wall anchored by a 80 × 120 cm tempered‑glass mirror that offers a clear view of the occupant as they stand at the front gate. Four bedrooms, a single bathroom, and a modest kitchen with painted‑wood cabinets occupy the rectangular plan, all finished with oak hardwood floors and white drywall. The structural system consists of a reinforced‑concrete slab, timber joists, and 2×4 stud walls, all tied together with steel brackets for the mirror. The house reads as a tidy, well‑proportioned colonial bungalow, its white façade and shingled roof presenting a timeless streetscape while the interior mirror adds a functional, reflective focal point.

Develop construction documents, specifying wood‑siding walls, asphalt‑shingle roof, and the mirror’s mounting hardware.
Excavate, pour a concrete slab foundation, and install perimeter footings to support the wood frame.
Erect the timber frame, sheathe walls, install windows, doors, interior finishes, and finally mount the glass mirror on the front‑hall wall.
Conduct a final inspection, verify that the mirror is securely fixed, and issue a certificate of occupancy.

The roof type defaults to asphalt shingles, the most common roofing material for the referenced designs.
